title: 180. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving One-Step Linear Equations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a one-step linear equation involving addition.
questions.question: Solve \(x+5=12\).
questions.explanation:
To isolate \(x\), subtract \(5\) from both sides:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x+5-5 &= 12-5\\
x &= 7
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x=7\).
questions.hint: Use the inverse operation of addition.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a one-step linear equation involving subtraction.
questions.question: Solve \(x-4=9\).
questions.explanation:
Add \(4\) to both sides to undo the subtraction:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x-4+4 &= 9+4\\
x &= 13
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x=13\).
questions.hint: Use the inverse operation of subtraction.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a one-step linear equation involving multiplication.
questions.question: Solve \(3x=18\).
questions.explanation:
Divide both sides by \(3\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{3x}{3} &= \frac{18}{3}\\
x &= 6
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x=6\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve a one-step linear equation involving division by a constant.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x}{4}=3\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply both sides by \(4\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
4\cdot \frac{x}{4} &= 4\cdot 3\\
x &= 12
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x=12\).
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by the denominator.

questions.concept: Solving One-Step Equations with a Negative Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Solve a one-step linear equation with a negative coefficient.
questions.question: Solve \(-2x=10\).
questions.explanation:
Divide both sides by \(-2\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{-2x}{-2} &= \frac{10}{-2}\\
x &= -5
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x=-5\).
questions.hint: Pay attention to the sign when dividing by a negative number.

questions.concept: Solving One-Step Subtraction Equations with a Negative Constant
questions.learningObjective: Solve a one-step linear equation written with subtraction.
questions.question: Solve \(x-3=-7\).
questions.explanation:
Add \(3\) to both sides:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x-3+3 &= -7+3\\
x &= -4
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x=-4\).
questions.hint: Add the same number to both sides to isolate \(x\), and be careful when adding a positive number to a negative number.

questions.concept: Solving One-Step Division Equations with a Negative Divisor
questions.learningObjective: Solve a one-step linear equation involving division by a negative number.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x}{-3}=4\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply both sides by \(-3\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
-3\cdot \frac{x}{-3} &= 4\cdot (-3)\\
x &= -12
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x=-12\).
questions.hint: Multiplying by a negative number changes the sign.

questions.concept: Solving One-Step Equations with the Variable on the Right
questions.learningObjective: Solve a one-step linear equation when the variable appears on the right side.
questions.question: Solve \(4=x-7\).
questions.explanation:
Add \(7\) to both sides:
\[
\begin{aligned}
4+7 &= x-7+7\\
11 &= x\\
x &= 11
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x=11\).
questions.hint: The equation can be rewritten as \(x-7=4\) if that helps.

questions.concept: Solving One-Step Equations with a Fractional Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Solve a one-step linear equation with a fractional coefficient.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{2}{3}x=6\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply both sides by the reciprocal of \(\frac{2}{3}\), which is \(\frac{3}{2}\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}x &= \frac{3}{2}\cdot 6\\
x &= 9
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x=9\).
questions.hint: Multiply by the reciprocal of the coefficient of \(x\).

questions.concept: Solving One-Step Equations with a Negative Variable
questions.learningObjective: Solve a one-step linear equation of the form \(-x=a\).
questions.question: Solve \(-x=8\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply both sides by \(-1\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(-1)(-x) &= (-1)(8)\\
x &= -8
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the solution is \(x=-8\).
questions.hint: Dividing or multiplying both sides by \(-1\) will isolate \(x\).
